name: getstackrun
description: Oversee the AI agents you run through STACK: check what they did, revoke their access and verify the audit log.

interface.longDescription:
STACK runs between AI agents and the systems they use. Each agent works under a short-lived Passport that states what it may do. STACK checks every call against that Passport, records suspicious behavior, can deny configured actions and writes each decision to a hash-chained audit log.

This connector brings the oversight side of STACK into the conversation. With it you can:
- list your agents, their permissions and any that are blocked
- see active Passports and revoke one, every Passport for an agent, or all of them
- decide flagged Passport checkouts waiting for review
- open, complete or revoke Missions and see what an agent did inside one
- read the audit log, verify its hash chain and export signed records
- list security events, adjust detector and PII-redaction settings, and scan text for prompt injection
- manage notification rules, inbound webhooks, drop-offs and fleets
- check usage

A revocation applies to the agent's next call through STACK and cascades to any Passports it delegated.

The connector does not call third-party services, connect or display credentials, issue Passports or run paid skills. Those stay in the STACK Console, the CLI and STACK's full MCP endpoint. Sign-in uses OAuth, and a token issued to this connector is refused by the full endpoint.

STACK's application services run in Stockholm and its database runs in Frankfurt.

Requires a STACK account with at least one registered agent. Setup: https://getstack.run/docs/mcp-setup#directory

Show the flagged checkouts waiting for review and summarize what each agent did.
Verify my audit log's hash chain and list today's security events.

positive.description: See which agents are blocked and why
positive.prompt: Which of my agents are blocked right now, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the account's agents and names the blocked agent (quarantine-bot) with its recorded block reason.

positive.prompt: List the Passports that are active right now.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the active (unexpired, unrevoked) Passports, including those held by review-demo.

positive.prompt: Revoke every active Passport for the review-demo agent.
positive.expected_behavior: Confirms the revocation. A follow-up list shows no active Passports for review-demo.

positive.prompt: Show the flagged checkouts waiting for review and block the first one.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the flagged checkout with its flags and records a block; that agent shows as blocked with the reason.

positive.prompt: Verify my audit log's hash chain.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns valid: true with the number of entries checked.

negative.prompt: What's the weather in Stockholm tomorrow?
Save my OpenAI API key in STACK.
Call the Stripe API and refund order 1042.

publication.release_notes: First release. Oversight tools for AI agents run through STACK: agents, Passports, review decisions, Missions, audit log, detectors, notifications and usage.
